div.div: Origin = scheme + host + port. A cookie is scoped by none of those three — it is scoped by Domain and Path.

div.div: 2 · Path — an axis localStorage does not have at all

div.div: The path prefix decides which requests carry it. Narrowing Path shrinks the blast radius of a leak.

div.div: Path is not part of an origin, so every page on the host reads the same store. There is no narrowing it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 543px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: One sentence to say out loud: the Storage APIs are scoped to an origin and never leave the browser; a cookie is scoped to a domain and a path and is attached to every matching request. That is why the token lives in the cookie and the dark-mode flag lives in localStorage.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
